title: 2-week plan for 3 finals + a paper
scenario: Two weeks until finals: Cognitive Psych (memorisation-heavy), Stats (problem-solving), Research Methods (essay paper, 3000 words), and Social Psych (concepts + applications). You haven't started the paper. You sleep 6 hours, gym 4 days a week, hate revising the day before, and learn best when you teach the material to someone (or a wall). You want a plan that respects this, not a generic ‘study 8 hours a day’.
badPrompt: make a 2-week study plan for my finals
badOutput: Week 1: Review notes for all subjects, create flashcards, start the paper outline. Week 2: Practice problems, write the paper, review weak areas. Study 6-8 hours daily. Take breaks. Get enough sleep.

hints.title: Tell Claude how you actually learn
hints.body: ‘Learn best by teaching it to a wall. Hate day-before cramming.’ Plans that ignore your learning style fail.

hints.title: Differentiate study type per subject
hints.body: Cognitive = memorisation, Stats = problem-solving, Research = writing. AI defaults to ‘review notes’ for everything.

checks.tip: Anchor the deliverables, 3 finals + a paper.
Name the subjects so Claude can differentiate study type.
Anchor the paper, 3000 words, not started.
Anchor your fixed constraints, sleep, gym days.
Reference your learning style, teaching to a wall.
Force differentiated study by subject type, not blanket review.
Surface ‘hate day-before cramming’ so plan front-loads work.
Specify a day-by-day grid, not prose.
Demand milestones (paper outline by day 3, etc.), not just topics.

tipIfLow: Study plans from AI are generic because they don't know how you learn. The unlock is anchoring your real constraints (sleep, gym), your learning style (teaching to a wall), AND differentiating study type per subject. Cognitive psych and Stats need different plans, not the same ‘review notes’.
goldPrompt: Act as a study coach who knows my specific brain. I'm Zara, 3rd-year psych. 2 weeks to: Cognitive Psych (memorisation), Stats (problem-solving), Research Methods paper (3000 words), Social Psych (concepts + applications). I sleep 6 hrs, gym 4 days/week, hate day-before cramming, learn best by teaching to a wall. Output a daily schedule that: (a) treats the 4 subjects with DIFFERENT methods (not 'review notes' for all), (b) embeds 'teach-it-out-loud' blocks for cog-psych and social-psych, (c) protects gym days, (d) starts the paper today not week 2, (e) ends day-before with rest, not cramming.
